sections.name: Perspectives in Psychology
tips: Exam-style questions from Phineas's kit for this deck. Read every choice before you pick: the wrong ones are common mix-ups.

questions.stem: Antonio is feeling much healthier now that he is focusing on his positive traits and having good relationships. Which perspective fits best?
questions.exp: Positivity, relationships, and well-being are humanistic.

questions.stem: Which perspective is based heavily on the ideas of Freud?
questions.exp: Psychodynamic: the unconscious mind and childhood experiences.

questions.stem: Which perspective focuses on genetics, brain chemistry, hormones, and neurotransmitters?
questions.exp: That's the biological perspective. Evolutionary is about survival and reproduction.

questions.stem: Which perspective emphasizes memory, problem solving, intelligence, and perception?
questions.exp: Cognitive = internal thought processes.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the behavioral perspective?
options: Behavior comes from the unconscious mind.
Behavior is mostly determined by genes.
Behavior depends on a person's culture.
Behavior is shaped by learned experiences, and rewarded behaviors tend to be repeated.
questions.exp: Behavioral = learning and rewards.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the evolutionary perspective?
options: Behavior is shaped by childhood memories.
Behaviors exist because they helped our ancestors survive and reproduce.
Behavior is shaped by social norms.
Behavior depends on how we think about situations.
questions.exp: Evolutionary = protection, adaptive behavior, and reproduction.

questions.stem: Charles has a terrible fear of spiders. Which explanation fits the evolutionary perspective?
options: Fearing spiders helped his ancestors avoid dangerous bites and survive.
A frightening spider experience from early childhood is affecting him unconsciously.
His thoughts about spiders are exaggerated and unrealistic.
In his culture, spiders are treated as scary and disgusting.
questions.exp: Survival advantage for ancestors = evolutionary. The others are psychodynamic, cognitive, and sociocultural.

questions.stem: Charles has a terrible fear of spiders. Which explanation fits the psychodynamic perspective?
options: Fearing spiders helped his ancestors survive.
His brain chemistry makes him more anxious.
People around him taught him spiders are gross.
A frightening spider experience from early childhood is affecting him unconsciously.
questions.exp: Unconscious mind + childhood = psychodynamic.

questions.stem: Charles has a terrible fear of spiders. Which explanation fits the cognitive perspective?
options: He believes every spider he sees could kill him, and those thoughts drive his fear.
He inherited a gene linked to anxiety.
In his culture, spiders are seen as dangerous.
He has an unconscious memory of being bitten.
questions.exp: Cognitive = how thought processes shape behavior.

questions.stem: Charles has a terrible fear of spiders. Which explanation fits the sociocultural perspective?
options: Fearing spiders helped his ancestors survive.
He focuses on his potential to overcome fear.
In his culture, spiders are commonly treated as scary and disgusting.
questions.exp: Culture or way of life = sociocultural.

questions.stem: Suzanne loves romantic comedy movies. Which explanation uses the biological perspective?
options: In her culture, it's popular for women to enjoy romantic movies.
She was often taken to romantic movies as a child.
Watching them causes her brain to release feel-good chemicals like dopamine.
She enjoys predicting how the plot will turn out.
questions.exp: Brain chemistry and neurotransmitters = biological. The culture answer is your slide's sociocultural example.

questions.stem: A therapist helps a client focus on free will, self-actualization, and reaching their full potential. Which perspective is the therapist using?
questions.exp: Free will, self-efficacy, and self-actualization are humanistic.

questions.stem: A psychologist argues that a teen's aggression is mostly due to high testosterone levels. Which perspective is this?
questions.exp: Hormones = biological.

questions.stem: A researcher compares how families in different countries discipline their children, expecting differences based on each country's way of life. Which perspective is this?
questions.exp: Differences based on culture or way of life = sociocultural.

questions.stem: Which of the following best explains why psychologists use different perspectives?
options: Only one perspective can be correct.
Each perspective is used for only one type of behavior.
Each one is like a different set of lenses, giving a different explanation of the same behavior.
Perspectives are only used to diagnose disorders.
questions.exp: Your slides: perspectives are like viewing situations through different lenses. A behavior can be explained by several.

sections.name: Research Methods
tips: Exam-style questions from Phineas's kit for this deck. Read every choice before you pick: the wrong ones are common mix-ups.

questions.stem: Which of the following best explains why psychologists rely on research instead of intuition?
options: Intuition is distorted by hindsight bias, overconfidence, and misunderstanding of probability.
questions.exp: Your slides: psychology exists because intuition is unreliable, due to hindsight bias, misunderstanding of probability, and overconfidence.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the correct order of the first four steps of the scientific method?
options: Observe → develop a theory → make a hypothesis → test it
Make a hypothesis → observe → replicate → develop a theory
Test → observe → develop a theory → evaluate
Develop a theory → replicate → observe → make a hypothesis
questions.exp: Observe, theory, hypothesis, test, evaluate, modify, replicate.

questions.stem: A researcher decides that "smiling" means at least four teeth showing and "friendly" means the photographer tells at least two jokes. These are:
questions.exp: Operational definitions state exactly how each variable will be measured.

questions.stem: Which of the following best explains why operational definitions are important?
options: Without them, other researchers can't replicate the study.
They guarantee the hypothesis will be supported.
They replace the need for a control group.
questions.exp: Your slides: research cannot be replicated without operational definitions.

questions.stem: A researcher repeats another scientist's study with new participants to see whether the results hold up. This is:
questions.exp: Replicating means doing the research a second time to check that the results are reliable.

questions.stem: Which research method is the only one that can establish cause and effect?
questions.exp: Experiments manipulate variables to establish cause and effect.

questions.stem: A psychologist spends two years studying one patient with a rare memory disorder in great detail. Which of the following is the biggest weakness of this method?
options: It gives too little in-depth information.
The findings may not apply to others, because the patient may be atypical.
questions.exp: Case studies can be misleading if the person is atypical, and can lead to overgeneralizing.

questions.stem: A researcher wants to know how 2,000 teens feel about social media and needs results quickly. Which method fits best?
questions.exp: Surveys collect a lot of self-reported data in a short time.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a disadvantage of naturalistic observation?
options: Subjects behave less honestly than in a lab.
Subjects may notice the observer and act differently.
questions.exp: It's non-invasive, but subjects may become aware of the observer, and it can be time consuming.

questions.stem: As hours of sleep decrease, levels of stress increase. Which type of correlation is this?
questions.exp: One goes down while the other goes up: negative.

questions.stem: As salary decreases, spending also decreases. Which type of correlation is this?
questions.exp: Both move in the same direction (both decrease), so it's positive. Positive doesn't mean "good."

questions.stem: Which correlation coefficient shows the strongest relationship?
questions.exp: Strength is how close the number is to +1 or -1. The sign only shows direction.

questions.stem: A study finds that students who eat breakfast earn higher grades. Which conclusion is most appropriate?
options: Higher grades cause students to eat breakfast.
Breakfast and grades are related, but the study can't show that breakfast causes better grades.
There is no relationship between them.
questions.exp: Correlation does not equal causation. Another factor could explain both.

questions.stem: Ice cream sales and sunburns rise together. According to your slides, which of the following best explains this?
options: Sunburns make people buy ice cream.
Hot, sunny summer weather causes both.
questions.exp: A third factor (summer weather) causes both, so they're correlated without one causing the other.

questions.stem: A researcher randomly picks 500 names from a list of every student in a school, so every student has an equal chance of being chosen. This is a:
questions.exp: Everyone having an equal chance of inclusion makes it a representative random sample. The whole school is the population.

questions.stem: Plants are randomly put in a room with music or a silent room, and their height is measured after a month. What is the independent variable?
questions.exp: The IV is what the researcher manipulates.

questions.stem: In the same plant study, what is the dependent variable?
questions.exp: The DV is what gets measured.

questions.stem: A study tests whether exercise causes weight loss, but the exercise group also happened to eat healthier food. Diet is a:
questions.exp: An outside influence that affects the results is a confounding variable. Your slides list diet, sleep, and genetics for this exact example.

questions.stem: Patients given a sugar pill they believe is a pain medication report feeling less pain. This is the:
questions.exp: Results caused by expectations alone are the placebo effect.

questions.stem: A horoscope says, "You sometimes doubt yourself, but you have hidden strengths," and Mia thinks it describes her perfectly. This is the:
questions.exp: Believing a general description applies specifically to you is the Barnum effect.

questions.stem: After a coin lands heads five times in a row, Leo bets on tails because tails is "due." This is:
questions.exp: Seeing patterns in random data is the gambler's fallacy. Each flip is still 50/50.

questions.stem: A survey asks, "Don't you agree that dangerous video games should be banned?" The biggest problem with this question is:
questions.exp: The wording pushes people toward one answer.

questions.stem: A researcher studying the exercise habits of all Americans surveys only members of one gym. The main problem is:
questions.exp: The sample doesn't represent the population, so the results will be skewed.

questions.stem: Before a study begins, participants are told what it involves so they can decide whether to take part. This is:
questions.exp: Informed consent comes before; debriefing comes after.

questions.stem: Which of the following would violate the APA's ethical guidelines?
options: Letting people choose whether to participate
Publishing participants' names and personal answers without permission
Getting approval from a research institution
questions.exp: That breaks confidentiality. The other three are required guidelines.

questions.stem: Overconfidence is best described as:
options: Believing you knew the outcome all along
Giving answers that make you look good
questions.exp: The others are hindsight bias, gambler's fallacy, and social desirability bias.

questions.stem: Participants in a study answer questions in ways they think the researcher wants, or exaggerate how good they are. This is:
questions.exp: Self-report bias: trying to affect the outcome, please the researcher, or being unrealistic about yourself.

sections.name: Statistics & Data
tips: Exam-style questions from Phineas's kit for this deck. Read every choice before you pick: the wrong ones are common mix-ups.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the purpose of descriptive statistics?
options: To decide whether results apply to a whole population
To organize and summarize data meaningfully
questions.exp: Descriptive statistics organize data. Deciding whether results generalize is inferential statistics.

questions.stem: Which type of graph is a bar graph that shows a frequency distribution?
questions.exp: Histograms show frequency distributions and make patterns quick to spot.

questions.stem: What is the mean of 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13?
What is the median of 4, 10, 6, 2, 8, 12?
questions.exp: In order: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. The two middle numbers are 6 and 8, so the median is (6 + 8) ÷ 2 = 7.

questions.stem: For the data 2, 3, 3, 5, 9, 9, 9, 12, which statement is correct?
questions.exp: 9 appears most (mode). Middle two are 5 and 9, so the median is 7. Sum is 52, and 52 ÷ 8 = 6.5.

questions.stem: Scores: 55, 70, 70, 85, 100. What is the range?
questions.exp: 100 − 55 = 45. (70 is the mode and median; 76 is the mean.)

questions.stem: Which of the following best explains why standard deviation is a more useful measure of variation than the range?
options: It shows the most common score.
It shows how much all the scores vary around the mean, not just the gap between the two extremes.
It is always smaller than the mean.
questions.exp: The range only uses the highest and lowest scores, so it's just a rough estimate.

questions.stem: Class A and Class B both averaged 80 on a test. Class A's standard deviation is 3; Class B's is 15. Which statement is true?
options: Class A's scores are more spread out.
Class B's scores are more spread out.
Class B scored higher on average.
Both classes have the same spread.
questions.exp: A bigger standard deviation means scores are more dispersed around the mean.

questions.stem: IQ scores have a mean of 100 and a standard deviation of 15. About what percent of people score between 85 and 115?
questions.exp: 85–115 is within 1 standard deviation of the mean: about 68%.

questions.stem: On the same IQ scale, about 95% of people score between:
questions.exp: Within 2 standard deviations (2 × 15 = 30 points) of 100.

questions.stem: A billionaire moves into a small town where most families earn very little. Which measure best describes a typical family's income?
questions.exp: The outlier pulls the mean way up. Your slides say the median and mode give a fuller picture.

questions.stem: Which statement is true of a positively skewed distribution?
options: The tail goes to the left
questions.exp: Positive skew: tail to the right, and the mean follows the tail.

questions.stem: In a negatively skewed distribution, the tail points:
options: Right, and the mean is pulled right
Left, and the mean is pulled left
Left, and the mode is pulled left
questions.exp: Negative skew = tail to the left. The mean always follows the tail.

questions.stem: Most families in a town earn $20,000–$50,000, but a few earn millions. How is income in this town distributed?
questions.exp: A few very high values make a tail to the right: positive skew.

questions.stem: A graph of the heights of a group of kindergartners and their parents has two clear peaks. This is a:
questions.exp: "Bi" means two: two peaks = bimodal.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes inferential statistics?
options: They measure how spread out scores are.
They help determine whether results can be generalized to a larger population.
questions.exp: Inferential statistics check that results aren't just chance fluctuations in the sample.

questions.stem: Which is one of the three key principles of inferential statistics on your slides?
options: Bigger samples are better than small ones.
Fewer estimates are better than more estimates.
Unrepresentative samples are better than representative ones.
One study is enough to generalize.
questions.exp: The three: representative samples, bigger samples, and more estimates are better.

questions.stem: Why is meta-analysis useful?
options: It studies one person in depth.
It removes the need for a sample.
It guarantees that results are significant.
It combines the estimates of many studies instead of relying on just one.
questions.exp: More estimates are better than fewer estimates.

questions.stem: Alex asks two friends about each café and decides Café Mocha is better. Which of the following best explains why her conclusion isn't reliable?
options: Her sample is small and unrepresentative.
Her effect size is too large.
questions.exp: Your slide names both problems: unrepresentative samples and small sample size.

questions.stem: A study reports p = .20. Which conclusion is correct?
options: The result is not statistically significant; it could easily be due to chance.
The result is significant because .20 is small.
questions.exp: Significant means p ≤ .05. .20 is too high.

questions.stem: Which statement about p-values and effect size is correct?
options: Effect size tells whether a result is due to chance.
A p-value tells whether an effect likely exists; effect size tells how strong it is.
A larger p-value means a stronger effect.
questions.exp: Your slides: unlike p-values, effect size tells how strong the effect is.

questions.stem: Students using a new study technique averaged 85; students studying as usual averaged 75. According to your slides, the 10-point difference is the:
questions.exp: Effect size shows the practical importance of the result: 85 − 75 = 10.

questions.stem: Ty is in the 70th percentile on a psychology test. This means:
options: He got 70% of the questions right.
He scored higher than 70% of his peers.
70% of students scored higher than him.
questions.exp: Percentile rank = the percentage of scores below yours.

examTips: Turn the Timer on and answer every question without looking anything up.
Aim for about one minute per question. Flag hard ones and come back.
